outcome: Neonatal anthropometric measurements (fetal weight, head circumference, femur length, large for gestational age, small for gestational age)
cohort: 1,000 mothers were enrolled and categorized into four groups based on their pre-pregnancy BMI.
finding: Both low and high pre-pregnancy BMI are associated with adverse maternal outcomes (gestational diabetes, hypertensive complications, cesarean sections) and perinatal outcomes (specific neonatal anthropometric measurements, prematurity, post-term birth, low birth weight).
mod_finding: Overweight and obese women were at a higher risk of undergoing cesarean sections.
cross-section timing: Data was collected from July 2010 to July 2011.
